answer.label: Not Oppenheimer — adapted from Cabell
answer.sourceLine: Wikiquote identifies the supposed Oppenheimer line as a version of James Branch Cabell’s The Silver Stallion. Cabell’s sentence uses “proclaims” and “we live,” rather than the circulating version’s “thinks this is.” Source and attribution evidence ↗

source.heading: The source
source.excerpt: The optimist proclaims that we live in the best of all possible worlds; and the pessimist fears this is true.
trail: Wikiquote identifies the supposed Oppenheimer line as a version of James Branch Cabell’s The Silver Stallion. Cabell’s sentence uses “proclaims” and “we live,” rather than the circulating version’s “thinks this is.” Source and attribution evidence ↗

The documented wording is a literary paradox: the optimist’s ideal world becomes the pessimist’s nightmare. The correction should retain the wording distinction as well as reassigning the source. Read the supporting source ↗
source.excerptNote: Documented wording; compare the popular version at the top.
source.rightsNote: The documented original comes from a work published before 1931 and is in the US public domain. This does not automatically license a later adaptation or a new edition’s additions.

schema.faqAnswer: The earlier documented aphorism is James Branch Cabell’s wording in The Silver Stallion (1926). The popular sentence is a modified version and is not established as an Oppenheimer quotation. This correction concerns the attributed origin and wording, not the truth of the philosophical observation.
